comments: This is the "innocent" meaning of the word hentai. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 変態する means transform or metamorphose, while enabling the following misunderstanding of 'pervert.' The English makes Taichi actively corrupt an already 'awful nature,' adding moral content and losing the intended transformation.

adjudicated.assessment: マイ言語 jokingly means a private language of their own. 'Selflanguage' is an opaque nonword and needs a space or idiomatic compound.

adjudicated.assessment: Miki describes the prospective consequence: it would be like founding a country without an army. The English says this outcome already happened.

adjudicated.jp: 「……うん。それでもう無理だと思って」

adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: ノイローゼ気味 describes signs of mental strain or neurosis. Calling the person herself 'neurotic' can read as a broader character judgment.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That one comes just out of nowhere, bam, no warning."
comments: {Ae}stethics -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that she appears from nowhere. The emphatic sound effect and explicit lack of warning are additions.

adjudicated.jp: 「ヒーローみたいですね」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Just like a hero, then."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

comments: If she's the hero, he's the heroine. So the villain... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi jokes that he is the heroine. The English uses an ungrammatical possessive construction and fails to state that equation.

adjudicated.jp: 「女顔してます」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Your face does look girly!"
comments: See CCC3010, CCA0011C (but it's all over, really). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……これでいい目見たこと一度もないです」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...that I've never seen as something lucky not once."
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says his feminine face has never once done him any good. The English is an ungrammatical relative fragment and does not convey that lack of benefit.

highlights.text: that I've never seen as something lucky not once

adjudicated.jp: 「怯えられたり押し倒されたり混乱されたり」

adjudicated.en: Miki: "What?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...because it's something necessary."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.assessment: The construction is ungrammatical, and the general consequence 'you die' is changed into a future progressive event.

highlights.text: if you don't eat, thing is, you'll be dying

adjudicated.jp: 「心の中でいろいろありまして、食う方に流れたわけだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "There's many things inside of the heart, and they flow there based on the ways you eat."
comments: See CCA0018B. What's for eating... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Taichi says that various things happened in his heart and he consequently came down on the side of eating. The English makes plural things flow somewhere according to methods of eating.

highlights.text: There's many things inside of the heart, and they flow there based on the ways you eat

adjudicated.jp: 「人が俺に対してよからぬことを考えるのは、顔のせいだと思った。わけもわからず気になったのは、目だな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I thought that it was the face to blame for why people don't think good of me. And I don't understand why, but my eyes keep bothering me."
comments: See CCA0021. These are indeed Mystic Eyes. Also CCD2002 - witches! And Miki's a witch... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The first clause is ungrammatical, while the second should say that what inexplicably bothered him was other people's eyes or gaze; the English instead suggests his own eyes are physically troubling him.

highlights.text: people don't think good of me. And I don't understand why, but my eyes keep bothering me

adjudicated.en: Miki: "Eyes?"
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「目が他人と違う気がして……いや、顔の造作も普通じゃないような気がして……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It feels like my eyes are different from that of others... no, it also feels like my facial features aren't normal..."
comments: What were they talking about again...? Sometimes Tanaka just seems to get lost. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The plural 'eyes' cannot be compared with the singular pronoun 'that'; the number must agree.

highlights.text: my eyes are different from that of others

adjudicated.jp: 「小ぎれいですよ。いわゆるハンサムではないですが」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "They're trim and pretty. Not what you would call 'handsome' however."
adjudicated.assessment: Miki describes Taichi's face as neat or pretty. The plural pronoun instead points back to his eyes.

adjudicated.jp: 「皆、そう言ってくれるけどね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "That's just what everybody tells me."
comments: That his face his pretty, not that he's handsome. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ははあ、ソレが先輩の心の傷ってやつですか」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Hah-ah... is that the wound on your heart, Senpai?"
adjudicated.assessment: The Japanese status address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

adjudicated.jp: 「んー、こんなのはオマケのオマケみたいなもので、本当は……」

comments: Yes, it totally is. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: オマケのオマケ calls this a mere extra on top of an extra, minimizing its importance. 'Cherry on top' normally presents a positive culminating bonus and reverses that force.

highlights.text: the cherry on top of the cherry on top

adjudicated.jp: こらこら、と自分を諫める。
adjudicated.en: Come on!, come on!, I remonstrate myself.
comments: No talking about the truth. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The verb requires 'with' before its object in this sense, and the source is simply self-admonition.

adjudicated.jp: 「とにかく取り引きなんで、曜子ちゃんに手を引いてもらうために霧は無力でいなければならないわけです」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, on to proper business. For purposes of getting Youko-chan to withdraw, it is absolutely imperative that Kiri remain free of offensive power."
comments: Suddenly formal. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: とにかく取り引きなんで means that this is, in any case, a deal or bargain. The English instead announces a transition to business and retains a Japanese diminutive address later in the sentence.

adjudicated.jp: 「話飛びーの」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "The conversation's so juuumpy."
comments: She notices the disconnection... maybe all the ones above too? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「ということで霧ちん借ります」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "And therefore, I shall be borrowing Kiri-chin."
adjudicated.assessment: The diminutive Japanese address remains untranslated rather than being represented in English.

adjudicated.jp: 「あのう……いじめないでやってくださいね？　いじりがいはあると思いますが」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Ah, uhm... please don't tease her OK? I do think she's fun to tease, but..."
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「……善処します」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...I will use my discretion."
comments: PCP CCC3010
Oh look, now it's a direct reference to that scene... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: 「なら、わたしもつきあいます」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "In that case I will be joining in, too."
comments: Since it means "I'll be messing around her"... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The English is supportable by the bound Japanese source in this unit.

adjudicated.jp: こうして。
adjudicated.en: And this,
